Pretty sure that this use of the word, "prompt", would have been incorrect a decade ago. But I see the dictionaries already seem to have incorporated it into the definitions.

PROMPT - 

Original definition as it pertains to computers - 

_5 Computers.
(of a computer system) to send a message or symbol to (a user) requesting information or instructions, usually by displaying the message or symbol on a screen:
Once the home page has loaded, the computer will prompt you to log in to your account_ .

The computer prompts the user. The user does not type a prompt but instead they type at a prompt or in response to the prompt. That which is typed is the command and specificities thereof - the details of exactly what the result should be - are described with parameters.

New fangled definition I'm pretty sure wasn't there before and as used with AI - 

_6 Computers, Digital Technology.
to request particular output from (a machine learning algorithm) by means of instructions, questions, examples, context, or other input_ .

This last bit would correctly have been the command and parameters typed at the prompt and specifying the desired result. The command and its associated parameters would  not be the prompt. They are typed in response to the prompt. The computer prompts the user for input. As newly defined in response to AI, this constitutes a misinterpretation of the original definition. But I guess it's official now.
